title: Usage-pattern Adjustment and Proforma Billing Playbook
author: Ravi Kapoor
content:
Purpose

This playbook documents the cross-functional operating procedure for: (1) detecting sustained shifts in customer usage patterns that materially affect committed capacity and billing; (2) issuing proforma invoices and estimate notices to customers; and (3) executing contract, procurement, and accounting follow-ups required for accurate revenue recognition. The intention is to reduce billing surprises, align forecasts with contractual terms, and preserve a complete audit trail for RevRec.

Scope

Applies to: Hosted API customers, Dedicated capacity customers, and Dedicated-to-Hosted migrations that create billing or recognition impacts. Exclusions: one-off refunds and routine invoice disputes (handled by Billing Ops exceptions). This playbook references the Commitment Usage Reconciliation SOP, Contract Amendment Guidance, and Procurement acceptance procedures.

Key definitions

- Usage spike: >30% month-over-month increase sustained for 3 consecutive weeks.
- Usage drop: >30% month-over-month reduction sustained for 3 consecutive weeks.
- Proforma invoice: a provisional, non-final invoice used to inform the customer of expected charges and to prompt commercial discussion.
- True-up window: the reconciliation period defined in the contract (monthly, quarterly, or annually).

Detection signals and ownership

1) Automated detection (Finance-Data owns):
   - Inputs: per-account per-model token counts, route-level meters, contract commit tiers, effective dates, and region mapping.
   - Rules (examples):
     - Alert A: sustained >30% MoM increase for 3 weeks OR a >=200% 7-day burst above baseline => "High-Usage Review".
     - Alert B: sustained >30% MoM decrease for 3 weeks => "Reduced-Usage Review".
   - Delivery: daily digest to Finance Ops Slack channel and creation of a triage ticket in the BillingOps queue.
2) Manual triggers: Sales, CS, or Platform may open a review when customers report traffic changes or migrations.

Initial triage (Finance Ops + Finance-Data + CS + Sales)

Checklist:
- Confirm measurement: run token audit and compare meter extraction to billing export.
- Confirm contract terms: check commit tier, auto-renew, minimums, and true-up cadence.
- Evaluate commercial impact: estimate delta vs. committed spend and enterprise discount breakpoints.
- Decide next step: monitor, issue proforma, or escalate to Sales + Legal for amendment.

Decision matrix (summary)

- Temporary spike (<7 days and <3x baseline): monitor; no proforma.
- Sustained spike (>=30% MoM for 3 weeks) or large burst (>=3x baseline): issue proforma and escalate Sales for contract review.
- Sustained drop with minimum commitment in contract: initiate credit/adjustment discussion with Legal and CS.
- Migration (Dedicated -> Hosted): run migration true-up flow and generate final proforma to reconcile remaining commitments.

Customer communication and timing

- Day 0: Triage ticket created with template "Usage-Adjustment-<YYYYMMDD>" including account ID, contract ID, observed deltas, and recommended action.
- Day 1-3: If escalation required, send initial proforma labeled "Estimate: Expected Charges" (non-binding) and request customer acknowledgement within 7 calendar days.
- Day 10-30: If unresolved and contract changes are needed, Sales to open amendment SOW and Legal to prepare redline.

Proforma invoice template (example)

---BEGIN PROFORMA---
Customer: {{customer_name}}
Account ID: {{account_id}}
Contract ID: {{contract_id}}
Period: {{start_date}} 14 {{end_date}}
Observed billable units: {{observed_tokens_or_hours}}
Contract committed units: {{committed_units}}
Estimated incremental charge (USD): {{estimated_incremental_usd}}
Notes: This is an informational estimate for planning and commercial discussion. Final billing subject to contractual terms and true-up reconciliation.
---END PROFORMA---

Contract and procurement follow-up patterns

1) Customer accepts increased usage as permanent:
   - Sales to draft contract amendment (use Contract Amendment checklist). Required items: new commit tier, effective date, termination/notice windows, price ladder, and audit rights.
   - Procurement/Finance: update committed spend in the master forecast and notify BillingOps/RevRec of the subscription delta.
2) Customer requests temporary burst:
   - Offer a burst purchase option (document via Order Form/PO) or use contracted burst bucket if available.
3) Customer disputes measurement:
   - Provide token accounting snapshot, RPC logs, and edge-proxy traces. Refer to the Tokenization Rules whitepaper for metering methodology.

Accounting and revenue recognition guidance

- General principle: prepaid committed capacity is recognized ratably over the committed term unless contractually satisfied earlier.
- When a proforma suggests probable incremental revenue but an amendment is not executed, create a forecast adjustment memo and notify RevRec: (a) update the 12-month revenue plan; (b) assess whether an allowance for variable consideration is required.
- Credits: any credit > $10,000 USD requires Finance VP approval and must include an audit packet (triage ticket, token audit, customer comms, Legal signoff).

Operational runbook (step-by-step)

1) Detection -> create triage ticket (Finance-Data).
2) Run measurement validation: finance-data-tools/token-audit.sh --account {{account_id}} --from {{start}} --to {{end}} and attach CSV output to ticket.
3) If validated and thresholds exceeded, create a "Proforma Request" task in BillingOps and assign Sales owner.
4) Finance Ops issues proforma (use template); set ProformaExpires = 30 days.
5) Sales engages commercial negotiation; Legal prepares amendment as needed.
6) After amendment/execution: BillingOps issues final invoice or credit memo; RevRec updates the recognition schedule or posts a deferral.

Example token-audit.sh (illustrative)

#!/bin/bash
# Example output format for playbook guidance
ACCOUNT=$1
FROM=$2
TO=$3
# CSV: date,route,tokens
echo "date,route,tokens"
echo "2026-10-01,generate-text,1245789"
echo "2026-10-02,chat-reply,987654"

Ownership and SLAs

- Finance-Data: detection pipeline development and daily alerting. SLA: 24 hours to acknowledge an alert.
- Finance Ops / Billing: proforma issuance and invoicing operations. SLA: 3 business days to issue proforma after triage validation.
- Sales: contract negotiation and amendment processing. SLA: initial draft within 10 business days.
- Legal: amendment review and approval. SLA: 5 business days for standard amendments.

Escalation rules

- Escalate to Director of Finance and Sales Lead when expected incremental charges exceed $50,000/month or when enterprise discount tiers are impacted.
- If measurement disputes remain unresolved after 10 business days, escalate to Head of Platform for deep technical validation and to Legal for contract interpretation.

Audit and recordkeeping

- Store all artifacts (proformas, triage tickets, token audits, amended contracts, final invoices/credits) in the BillingOps folder in the finance shared drive and link to the CLM contract record. Retention: 7 years.
- Audit packet checklist: triage ticket, token audit CSV, proforma sent, customer acknowledgement (email/PO), amendment (if any), final invoice/credit memo, and Legal signoff.

Metrics tracked (weekly dashboard)

- Number of proformas issued (target: < 5% of enterprise base per quarter).
- Mean time from detection to proforma issuance (target: <= 3 business days).
- Proforma-to-amendment conversion rate within 30 days (target: >= 60%).
- Total incremental revenue under review vs. forecast variance (dollar and percentage).
